answer: Personalized canary prompts catch farms that run many seats from one shared brain. Each epoch the network passes every task through a prism that splits it into per-seat variants, each hiding a unique canary detail, such as an invented tundra town name, shown to that seat alone. If seat A's canary turns up in seat B's answer, that leak is the signal that both draw on shared memory, and both forfeit the epoch. To stay clean, each extra fake needs its own fully isolated model context and operator, rebuilt every epoch because the variants are fresh.
